note: Capabilities shared by the ODC and O11 lanes. What is common lives once: identity, keywords, summary, route, contract pointers, the operations with their route and preconditions, guidance, the element roles. What differs lives under `platforms.<lane>` (proofs, negative jobs, limits with origin, reader context kinds, differences), under `elements[].platforms.<lane>` (native qualified type, job type name, address) and under `operations.<op>.roles.<role>.<lane>` (one statement per element ROLE and lane: status, proof jobs, negative jobs, the scope the proof established, observed behaviour whose integrity is not verified). A proof of one role never counts for another role (a record proof does not prove the entity), a proof of one lane never counts for the other, and a role not declared for an operation is undetermined. Statuses: applicable = proven by a positive job of that lane on that role (the answer downgrades it to declared-not-proven when no current result names the verb on the role's native type); conditional = works under the stated precondition (a refusal outside it is proven by the negative job); not-applicable = refused by the platform (proven), with the alternative; undetermined = not measured on that lane for that role. `observed` = behaviour that ran and was read back but whose integrity (leftovers, publication) is not verified: never applicability, never a recommendation. Nothing here is a signature: native types are checked against the lane runtime (api --op native) when the index is built, proofs against the lane suites, contract pointers against api --op of the lane CLI.

capabilities.guidance: Renaming an attribute rewrites the expressions that read it (Quote.Address.Zone -> Quote.Address.District); renaming the structure rewrites nothing because expressions cite parameters and attributes, not the type. capabilities.title: Entities, attributes, identifiers (foreign keys) and indexes: declare, read, edit, rename, repoint, reorder, duplicate, delete
capabilities.summary: Persistent server entities declared in one `spec` op (attributes with type/length/mandatory/default, foreign keys as the attribute type `<Entity> Identifier`, indexes with attributes and unique, public/readOnly, update behavior) and maintained afterwards by path (`IServerEntity:<Name>`, `IServerEntity:<Name>/<Attribute>`, `EntityIndex:<Name>`, `EntityIndex:<Name>/<Attribute>`) with the raw verbs. A relationship is not an element: it is the attribute whose DataType is `<Entity> Identifier`; the platform-generated child `<Entity> Identifier` (IIdentifierType) is what those attributes bind to, so `usages` of an entity under-reports its foreign keys. Every foreign key is born with its own AutoIndex_<Attribute> on both lanes.

route.operation: {"op":"spec","data":{"entities":[{"name":"Order","attributes":[{"name":"CustomerId","type":"Customer Identifier","mandatory":true}],"indexes":[{"name":"UQ_Order_Number","unique":true,"attributes":["Number"]}]}]}} to create; raw verbs (create IEntityAttribute + set DataType, create EntityIndex {args: {unique, attributes}}, set, rename, replace, move, duplicate, delete, usages, get/dump) by path to maintain

capabilities.guidance: Declare types and identifiers before the fields that use them: foreign keys between entities of the same spec never need separate jobs; declare data before the logic and screens that use it. To maintain an existing model, address elements by path, read before and after (get, dump, usages) and never trust the counters a verb returns. Renaming an entity or an attribute follows by key (expressions, SQL, aggregates, indexes, foreign-key types); Description, index names and text literals do not follow. Deleting a foreign key needs its AutoIndex deleted first; deleting an attribute with consumers is refused naming them (repoint with replace or remove them). Deleting the entity itself is not a proven path (the platform-generated `<Entity> Record` and `<Entity> List` cite it). Changing a type, a mandatory flag, a unique index or deleting a column executes headless: what it does to a published database with rows is not proven here. Index names are limited to 28 characters (the Studio truncates longer names silently; the kernel refuses them).
